_comments: THE HOURLY ACTIVITY SYNC. MJ's SchedulingEngine is the mechanism — no external cron anywhere in
this app.
The values below are the ones recorded in D-23, and each of the four non-obvious ones is a choice:
· JobTypeID  — the seeded `Action` type (ActionScheduledJobDriver). The job does not contain
logic; it invokes `Sales.SyncActivities`, which keeps the schedule and the work separable.
· CronExpression `0 0 * * * *` — SIX fields in this dialect, seconds first, so this is the top of
every hour. A five-field reading of the same string would be 'every minute of midnight', which
is why the seeded MJ jobs are worth comparing against before editing it.
· ConcurrencyMode `Skip` — a run overlapping its predecessor would fetch the same window twice.
Dedupe would absorb the writes, so the damage is wasted Graph calls rather than duplicate rows,
but two runs racing to advance the same watermark can leave it BEHIND where the earlier run got
to, which silently re-reads a window on the next pass.
· MissedRunPolicy `RunOnce` — not `RunAll`. Because there is no date filter on the fetch, catching
up ten missed hours would make ten identical requests for the most recent N messages. RunAll
would cost ten times as much to achieve exactly what one run achieves.
WHY IT IS SAFE TO SHIP `Active`. The action's default source is an EMPTY fixture, so an hourly run
reads the connections, applies the rules, calls the filter and writes nothing — reporting
`NO_CONNECTIONS` until somebody creates an ActivitySyncConnection, and zero-fetched after that until
somebody swaps the factory for a Graph-backed one. Neither state writes to LastError, so the
operator surface that exists to make a broken sync visible stays quiet until there is something
real to say.
OwnerUserID and NotifyUserID are deliberately left NULL: both are nullable, and naming a person here
would seed one deployment's staff into another's database.

fields.Name: Sales — Activity Sync (hourly)
fields.Description: Pulls Outlook messages and calendar items for every Active Microsoft365 sync connection and files the relevant ones as Activities against their deal. Writes nothing until a deployment supplies a real source; see the notes in this file.
